ops.name: admin.diagnostics
ops.desc: A bundle for a bug report with nothing private in it: version and build, system, the configuration's shape (an allow-list of settings; no secret, address, path or name), migrations, row counts per table, queue and job states, disk use by area, and the last warnings and errors with paths reduced to route patterns and anything token-like removed. No manuscript text, comment, email or name is in it.

config.description: Settings from an allow-list: numbers, switches and whether a setting is set. Never a secret, an address, a path or a name.

log.description: The last warnings and errors, newest last: a route pattern, a status, a short scrubbed message.

redacted.description: What was left out, in words.

ops.name: admin.diagnostics.download
ops.desc: The same bundle as a zip (diagnostics.json and a README), the same bytes for the same state.

body.description: The zip. The REST route returns it as the response body instead of JSON.

ops.name: admin.quota.list
ops.desc: What the instance and each person use against the limits that exist: attachment storage (per person, per project, whole instance, largest file) and API keys per person. Read only: the limits are set by the server's configuration, not per person.

editable.description: Always false: the limits are the server's configuration and have no per-person override.

projects.description: Projects owned (there is no limit on this).

ops.name: admin.user.disable
ops.desc: Switch a person off. They cannot sign in, every browser session of theirs ends now, their API keys and open streams stop working, and everything they wrote stays where it is (the projects they own stay theirs). Not yourself, and not the last administrator. Administrators only, browser session only; the screen asks you to type their name first.

member_of.description: Projects they are on without owning.

ops.name: admin.user.enable
ops.desc: Switch a person back on. Their keys work again; they sign in as before. Administrators only, browser session only.

member_of.description: Projects they are on without owning.

ops.name: admin.user.get
ops.desc: One person by id, as admin.user.list shows them. Administrators only.

member_of.description: Projects they are on without owning.

ops.name: admin.user.list
ops.desc: The people on this instance, for an administrator: name, email (an administrator sees it; nobody else does here), instance role, last seen, whether they are switched off, how many projects they own and are on, the storage they use and the browser sessions they have open. Agents are not listed. Filter by q (a word of the name or email) and status (all, active, disabled).

q.description: A word of the name or email.

status.description: Default all.

member_of.description: Projects they are on without owning.

ops.name: admin.user.set_role
ops.desc: Give or take away administration (role admin, or writer or reader for someone who is not one). Only where no administrator group is configured: with one, the identity provider decides at every sign-in and this is refused. Not the last administrator. Someone made a writer or reader here has their role set again from the identity provider's groups at their next sign-in. Administrators only, browser session only.

member_of.description: Projects they are on without owning.

ops.name: ai.accept.alternative
ops.desc: Add candidates of an alternatives run to an alternative (an existing one, or a new one over the text they were made for), as wordings with source generated. The text of the document does not change unless you name a candidate in choose. One transaction; revision checked.

alternative_id.description: Add them to this alternative. Empty: make an alternative over the text the run was made for (its original wording stays chosen).

candidate_ids.description: The candidates to add. Empty: every one still open.

choose.description: A candidate id to put in the text in the same save. Empty: the text does not change.

before.description: Up to 24 characters of Markdown before the anchor.

chosen_position.description: 1-based place of the chosen wording in the cycle.

quote.description: The chosen wording, which is what the anchored text says.

start.description: Where the anchored text starts, in UTF-16 code units of the body. Meaningless when orphaned.

status.description: orphaned: the text it was anchored to is gone or changed beyond recognition; its wordings are kept. Reattach it with alternative.reanchor.

original.description: The wording the text had when the alternative was made. It cannot be edited or removed.

source.description: manual: written by a person. generated: suggested by a configured provider (Phase 4).

comment.description: The alternatives comment that now ends the text ('' when there is none). An editor holding the document swaps its copy of that last line for this one.

content.description: The whole stored text, when with_content was set.

end.description: Where the replaced text ended before the change.

start.description: Where the replaced text started, in UTF-16 code units of the body.

revision.description: The document's revision after the write.

revision_id.description: The history entry written for a choice (reason alternative).

added.description: Candidates now wordings of the alternative, marked source generated.

skipped.description: Candidates already accepted or rejected before.

ops.name: ai.accept.edit
ops.desc: Accept one suggestion of a selection, chat or continue run: the server applies the text it holds for that run (never text you send) to the document, in one transaction, as one history entry with reason ai-accepted, with no word credit. The document revision you hold must be current (409 with the current revision otherwise); if the document changed in between, the suggestion applies only where its original text is still found exactly once with all the context it had (the words around it in its paragraph, and the paragraph's edges), and is a 409 otherwise. Accepting twice is harmless (applied false, already true). Refused while AI is off for the project.

base_revision.description: The revision of the document you hold. The suggestion applies to the text it was made from: if the document has changed, the suggestion is applied only where its original text is still found exactly once with all the context it had, and a 409 says so when it is not.

expect_hash.description: The text_hash of the suggestion you reviewed. A different text is refused.

run_id.description: The run that made the suggestion (its data.run_id).

tab_id.description: Browser tab id; enables the single-writer lease.

applied.description: False when this suggestion had already been accepted (already is then true): nothing was written.

comment.description: The alternatives comment that now ends the text, as alternative ops return it.

start.description: UTF-16 code units of the body before the change.

revision.description: The document's revision after the write.

revision_id.description: The history entry (reason ai-accepted); restoring the one before undoes the change.

ops.name: ai.accept.reject
ops.desc: Dismiss a suggestion or candidate of a run (or every open one). The held text is deleted once none is open.

suggestion_id.description: One suggestion or candidate. Empty: every one of the run that is still open.

open.description: Suggestions of the run still waiting.

ops.name: ai.budget.get
ops.desc: The monthly caps that apply to you (the instance's, yours, and with project_id that project's) and how much of each is used or held for requests in flight. Administrators also get every cap that was set. Works while AI is switched off: it sends nothing.

project_id.description: Also the caps of this project (you need access to it).

scope.description: Whose cap: the whole instance, you, the project (set by an administrator), or the project's owner's own cap.

month.description: YYYY-MM, UTC. Caps reset on the first of the month.

rows.description: Administrators only: every cap that was set.

subject.description: The user or project the cap is for; empty for the instance.

ops.name: ai.budget.set
ops.desc: Administrators, browser sessions only. Set a monthly cap for the instance, a person or a project, in tokens and in money (micro-units of the instance currency). 0 for both removes the cap. A cap is enforced before each request: a request that could take the month over it is refused.

max_cost_micros.description: Monthly, in micro-units of the instance currency (1,000,000 = one unit). 0: no money cap.

subject.description: The user or project id; empty for the instance.
The user or project the cap is for; empty for the instance.

ops.name: ai.chat.append
ops.desc: Add a finished exchange to a kept chat (after a streamed chat run): the answer must be the one the run produced; its hash is checked against the run record.

message.description: What you said, as you sent it. Up to 4,000 characters.

run_id.description: Your chat run (streamed or not). The answer must be the one that run produced: its hash is checked against the run's record.

content.description: Untrusted: show it as text.

ops.name: ai.chat.create
ops.desc: Keep a conversation: nothing is stored on the server unless you create a chat and add to it. A kept chat is yours alone, and deleted with ai.chat.delete.

title.description: Up to 100 characters.

content.description: Untrusted: show it as text.

ops.name: ai.chat.delete
ops.desc: Delete a kept chat and its messages. Works while AI is switched off: it sends nothing.

ops.name: ai.chat.get
ops.desc: One of your kept chats with its messages. Works while AI is switched off: it sends nothing.

content.description: Untrusted: show it as text.

ops.name: ai.chat.list
ops.desc: Your kept chats on the project. Works while AI is switched off: it sends nothing.

content.description: Untrusted: show it as text.

ops.name: ai.chat.preview
ops.desc: Preview one chat message exactly as ai.context.preview does, with the earlier messages taken from a kept chat. Writes nothing and calls no provider.

chat_id.description: A kept chat: its earlier messages are sent as the conversation and this exchange is added to it. Empty: nothing is kept; send turns yourself.

chips.description: Context chips for this message. Omit for the defaults (the selection, the brief, the style guide).

auto.description: For entities: also those whose name appears in the selection or the document.

document_id.description: For document, synopsis and previous_*: another document than the target.

ids.description: For entities and research: the ids.

text.description: For instruction: your own words, up to 4,000 characters.

nonce.description: Preview: leave empty. Send: the preview's.

base_revision.description: The document revision the range was read from. Required with start and end; a changed document is a 409.

before.description: With quote: source before it, to tell repeats apart.

occurrence.description: With quote: which occurrence (from 0), when context cannot tell.

quote.description: Instead of offsets: the Markdown source of the text.

start.description: Start of the range, in UTF-16 code units of the body.

turns.description: Earlier messages, when the chat is not kept.

body.description: The request body, byte for byte as it is sent to this provider. Its SHA-256, with the other attempts', is the payload hash.

max_tokens.description: After clamping to the model's limit.

scope.description: Whose cap: the whole instance, you, the project (set by an administrator), or the project's owner's own cap.

month.description: YYYY-MM, UTC. Caps reset on the first of the month.

redacted.description: Names in it are replaced by placeholders.

estimate_micros.description: Input plus a typical answer, in micro-units (1,000,000 = one unit of the currency).

known.description: False when no price is known: the cost is unknown, not zero.

local.description: The provider is local; the call costs nothing.

max_micros.description: Input plus the longest answer allowed: what is reserved against the budget.

code.description: policy_off, action_not_allowed, agents_not_allowed, no_provider, too_large, over_context, budget_exceeded, price_unknown.

input_tokens.description: Estimated; the provider's own count replaces it after the run.

nonce.description: Send it back with payload_hash to ai.run.

payload.description: The messages, provider-neutral: what a person reads. Each attempt's body is the same messages in that provider's own format.

redaction_mapping.description: Which names were replaced by which placeholders.

reserve_micros.description: The same in micro-units, for the instance's money; absent when no provider in the chain draws on it or a price is unknown.

reserve_tokens.description: The most this request can count against a token cap: its input once for every send the chain allows (each provider, each retry) plus the longest answer. What a run holds while it is running; the real usage replaces it.

ops.name: ai.chat.send
ops.desc: Send a previewed chat message (the preview's payload_hash and nonce are required, as for ai.run) and, for a kept chat, add the exchange to it. Not streamed: use the stream route with the chat recipe for a streamed answer and ai.chat.append afterwards. Nothing is inserted into the manuscript; a proposed wording for a selection is a suggestion for ai.accept.edit.

chat_id.description: A kept chat: its earlier messages are sent as the conversation and this exchange is added to it. Empty: nothing is kept; send turns yourself.

chips.description: Context chips for this message. Omit for the defaults (the selection, the brief, the style guide).

auto.description: For entities: also those whose name appears in the selection or the document.

document_id.description: For document, synopsis and previous_*: another document than the target.

ids.description: For entities and research: the ids.

text.description: For instruction: your own words, up to 4,000 characters.

nonce.description: Preview: leave empty. Send: the preview's.

base_revision.description: The document revision the range was read from. Required with start and end; a changed document is a 409.

before.description: With quote: source before it, to tell repeats apart.

occurrence.description: With quote: which occurrence (from 0), when context cannot tell.

quote.description: Instead of offsets: the Markdown source of the text.

start.description: Start of the range, in UTF-16 code units of the body.

turns.description: Earlier messages, when the chat is not kept.

attempts.description: Providers tried; more than one means a fallback was used.

data.description: The structured form, when the recipe parses one (notes, marks, JSON). Absent when the answer did not parse; the text is then all there is.

incomplete.description: The answer was cut off (length limit, cancellation or a broken stream).

status.description: ok; cancelled (the text so far is kept); error (only with text: a stream broke part way, and what arrived is kept).

text.description: What the model said, with redacted names put back. Untrusted text: show it as text, never as HTML.

unrestored_placeholders.description: Placeholders in the answer that did not match any name.

usage_reported.description: The counts are the provider's own; otherwise they are estimates.

ops.name: ai.context.preview
ops.desc: Build an AI request without sending it: the chips with their sizes, the exact request body for every provider that may receive it, the token and cost estimates, the redaction mapping, the policy and budget decision, and a payload_hash with a nonce. Writes nothing and calls no provider. The response holds manuscript text, so it is never kept for idempotent replay.

chips.description: Exactly what to include. Omit it to get the recipe's default chips; send an empty list to include none.

auto.description: For entities: also those whose name appears in the selection or the document.

document_id.description: For document, synopsis and previous_*: another document than the target.

ids.description: For entities and research: the ids.

text.description: For instruction: your own words, up to 4,000 characters.

document_id.description: The document the request is about.

max_tokens.description: Ask for a shorter answer than the recipe's limit. It is clamped to the recipe's, the model's and the server's limits.

model.description: With provider: the model. Empty: the provider's default.

nonce.description: Preview: leave empty to get one. Run: the nonce the preview returned.

payload_hash.description: Run: the payload_hash the preview returned. A run needs it.

provider.description: Use this provider alone (no chain). Empty: the project's or the instance's chain, then the first usable provider.

recipe.description: The recipe id; ai.recipe.list lists them.

base_revision.description: The document revision the range was read from. Required with start and end; a changed document is a 409.

before.description: With quote: source before it, to tell repeats apart.

occurrence.description: With quote: which occurrence (from 0), when context cannot tell.

quote.description: Instead of offsets: the Markdown source of the text.

start.description: Start of the range, in UTF-16 code units of the body.

stream.description: The request will be sent as a stream (ai/run/stream). It changes the bytes sent, so preview with the same value.

turns.description: Earlier messages of a chat, oldest first.

body.description: The request body, byte for byte as it is sent to this provider. Its SHA-256, with the other attempts', is the payload hash.

max_tokens.description: After clamping to the model's limit.

scope.description: Whose cap: the whole instance, you, the project (set by an administrator), or the project's owner's own cap.

ops.name: ai.defaults.get
ops.desc: The default provider chains per model class (cheap, strong, fast, local): the project's, yours and the instance's, and the one each class resolves to.

effective.description: For each class: what a recipe of that class uses when nothing more specific applies. The order is the request's own provider choice, then a chain the project names for the recipe or its action, then the project's class chain, your class chain, the instance's.

project.description: The project's chains by class, set by its owner (stored in the policy as class:<class>).

ops.name: ai.defaults.set
ops.desc: From a browser session only (it is configuration, like the policy). Set a default provider chain for a model class at one level: project (its owner), user (yourself) or instance (an administrator). Resolution: the request's own provider, then the project, then you, then the instance. A local-only project's chains may name only local providers. An empty chain removes the default.

chain.description: Providers and models to try in order, at most 6. Empty removes the default. A failure retrying can fix (timeout, 5xx, rate limit) moves to the next entry; a refusal never does.

class.description: The model class a recipe prefers (ai.recipe.list shows each recipe's).

scope.description: project: the project's owner. user: yourself. instance: an administrator.

effective.description: For each class: what a recipe of that class uses when nothing more specific applies. The order is the request's own provider choice, then a chain the project names for the recipe or its action, then the project's class chain, your class chain, the instance's.

project.description: The project's chains by class, set by its owner (stored in the policy as class:<class>).

ops.name: ai.exclude.list
ops.desc: What is flagged never-send in the project (entities as far as you may read them). Works while AI is switched off: it sends nothing.

ops.name: ai.exclude.set

ops.desc: One recorded merge or split with its before-state: every entity that moved (its name and revision as they were), every entity merged away with its whole sheet, every relationship, event person, place and alias that was dropped, the keys repointed and the references added. Owner.

id.description: Compendium id: the source or the target of the change.

summary.description: Counts of what the change did.

ops.name: compendium.change.list
ops.desc: The merges and splits that moved entities into or out of this Compendium, newest first: when, by whom, the counts. Owner.

summary.description: Counts of what the change did.

ops.name: compendium.create
ops.desc: Create a Compendium: the shared bible (entities, and later research and a timeline) for one story world or subject. It exists with or without a project. The caller becomes its owner. Pass project_id to make it the primary Compendium of a project the caller owns that has none; a project has at most one primary.

kind.description: Default fiction.

name.description: Up to 200 characters.

project_id.description: Make this the primary Compendium of a project the caller owns that has none yet.

starter_fields.description: Define the starter custom fields (a character's role, age, appearance, voice, wants, fears, secrets and arc; a place's region; and so on). Default true.

role.description: The caller's role: owner, editor or reader. An instance admin acts as owner.

ops.name: compendium.export
ops.desc: Export a Compendium as a Markdown bundle (a zip): one file per entity with front matter (name, kind, aliases, summary, custom fields, relationships), a manifest of the Compendium's settings, field definitions and every file's SHA-256, and a README. Deterministic: the same state gives the same bytes. Recorded with a manifest of what it held. Works with no project open. Editor.

body.description: The file. The REST route returns it as the response body instead of JSON.

entities.description: How many entities the export holds.

ops.name: compendium.get
ops.desc: Get one Compendium with what depends on it: the projects that use it (named only when the caller can open them), the Compendiums it references and how many reference it, and the member count.

role.description: The caller's role: owner, editor or reader. An instance admin acts as owner.

hidden_projects.description: Projects that use it and that the caller cannot open. Counted, never named.

projects.description: Projects the caller can open that use this Compendium. Deleting the Compendium removes it from all of them.

relation.description: primary: it is the project's primary Compendium. reference: the project references the whole Compendium.

referenced_by.description: How many other Compendiums reference this one.

references.description: Other Compendiums this one references, read-only. Only those the caller can read are listed; the rest are counted in hidden_references.

id.description: The reference id, for removing it.

ops.name: compendium.list
ops.desc: List the Compendiums the caller is a member of, most recently changed first. The default state is active (neither archived nor trashed). Returns at most 500; narrow with q or state.

state.description: active (default), archived, trashed or all. The trash view lists only Compendiums the caller owns.

role.description: The caller's role: owner, editor or reader. An instance admin acts as owner.

truncated.description: True when more than 500 matched and the rest were left out.

ops.name: compendium.member.add
ops.desc: Give a person access to a Compendium, as an editor or a reader. They must already have signed in to this instance; find them by exact email. An address nobody can be added under (unknown, removed, an API-only account, or a reader who cannot be an editor) all answer the same way, so this cannot be used to list who is here. A person already on the Compendium is refused, not changed; use compendium.member.update. Owner only.

ops.name: compendium.member.list
ops.desc: List who can open a Compendium and their roles. Owner only.

ops.name: compendium.member.remove
ops.desc: Take a person off a Compendium. Their project memberships are untouched, and so is anything they wrote. The owner cannot be removed. Owner only.

ops.name: compendium.member.update
ops.desc: Change a member's role (editor or reader). The owner's role cannot change. Owner only.

ops.name: compendium.merge
ops.desc: Move this Compendium's entities (all of them, or entity_ids) into another, in one transaction, keeping their ids: aliases, mentions, links, overrides and scenes follow. Name clashes are settled per entity in resolutions (a merge there is entity.merge, permanent); relationships and timeline events that would join the two are refused unless crossing is drop; API keys pinned to the source are refused unless key_pins says repoint or leave. fingerprint must be the one compendium.merge.preview returned. The before-state is recorded (compendium.change.get) and returned. The source Compendium is not deleted. Owner of both; refused for a Compendium in the trash.

crossing.description: What to do with relationships and timeline people that would join the two Compendiums: refuse (default) or drop them (kept in the before-state).

entity_ids.description: The entities to move; empty means every live entity of the source (a split needs them).

follow_projects.description: Add a read-only reference to the target to the projects that used the source, where the caller owns the project.

key_pins.description: API keys pinned to the source: refuse the move (default), repoint them to the target (widening them; only keys whose owner is on the target), or leave them pinned to the source.

action.description: rename: give it new_name. merge: merge it into into_id, an entity of the target (same kind), by entity.merge's rules. drop_aliases: move it and drop the aliases that clash (its name must not clash). skip: leave it in the source.

field_choices.description: For merge: source or target for each custom field both hold differently, as in entity.merge.

into_id.description: For merge: the entity of the target to merge into.

resolutions.description: By entity id: what to do with an entity whose name or alias the target already uses.

fingerprint.description: From the preview; required by compendium.merge.

aliases_blocked.description: Aliases of the source a third entity uses: dropped.

aliases_duplicate.description: Aliases of the source the target already has (or is named): dropped.

extra.description: Rows other features move with the merge, by feature.

choice.description: What the request chose: source or target; empty while unresolved.

fields_taken.description: Custom fields only the source had: copied to the target.

hidden_override_conflicts.description: Projects the caller cannot open that overrode both entities. They are not named and cannot be chosen for: the target's override is kept there.

links_dropped.description: Project links the target already had.

locked_override_conflicts.description: Projects the caller is on but has not unlocked (they have a passphrase) that overrode both entities. A real merge is refused while this is not zero: their source override would be deleted without anyone being able to see or choose it. Unlock them, then choose per project.

name_as_alias.description: The source's name, kept as an alias of the target; empty when not.

key.description: The field_choices key to answer with: override:<project id>.

overrides_dropped.description: Source overrides discarded: the request chose the target's, or the project is one the caller cannot open.

redirects_repointed.description: Older merged ids that now lead to the target.

reason.description: self: it would relate the target to itself. duplicate: the target already has the same relationship.

scene_refs_repointed.description: Scenes whose point of view or location was the source.

unresolved.description: field_choices keys still needing an answer. A real merge is refused while this is not empty.

fields.description: Custom field values by key, as canonical strings (a number as 34, a date as YYYY-MM-DD).

back_cover.description: EPUB: put the project's own back cover (project.cover_layout.get) last in the book, on a page of its own outside the reading order (default false). Only a layout that gives the back a picture, or a wrap, has one; the generated cover has no back page. Off when own_cover is false.

byline.description: The name on the title page, when it is not the project's author name (a pen name).

chapter_drop.description: How far down the page a chapter title starts, in inches, 0 to 5.

chapter_heading.description: What a chapter heading says: 'Chapter 3: Title', 'Chapter 3', the title alone, or nothing.

chapter_label.description: The word before a chapter number (default Chapter), up to 24 characters.

chapter_ornament.description: Print: the ornament under a chapter heading (default false). The ornament is the scene-break ornament.

chapter_start.description: Each chapter starts a new page, or (recto, PDF) on the next right-hand page with a blank page inserted when needed, or runs on.

clear.description: Options to reset to empty when this is laid over a preset: byline, header_title, ornament, language, chapter_label, imprint. An empty string in a field means 'not set', so this is how to clear one.

contact.description: DOCX manuscript title page: show your contact block (default true). false leaves the block off the page and leaves the word count top right.

copyright_page.description: Print: a copyright page after the title page (default true).

cover.description: EPUB: put the cover first: a cover page and the cover image the shops and readers use. It is the project's own cover when it has one (project.cover_layout.get), else the generated cover. Default true. KDP takes the cover as a separate upload and asks for no cover page in the file, so turn this off for a file bound for KDP.

cover_page.description: Print, for a proof or a copy you print yourself (default false): the cover's front as the first page of the PDF, edge to edge (into the bleed with crop marks), followed by a blank page so the title page stays a right-hand page. Do not upload a file made with it to a print-on-demand printer as the interior: KDP and IngramSpark take the cover as a separate file, and a printer counts and prints every page of the interior, so these two pages would be printed and would change the page count and the spine. The page count that export.cover and compile.cover_spec use does not include them. It is the project's own cover, or the generated one when there is none or own_cover is false. A right-to-left book has no PDF.

crop_marks.description: Print: a proof with crop marks: the page grows by a 0.125 inch bleed and a quarter-inch slug, the marks are drawn outside the trim and the trim and bleed boxes are set (default false).

drop_cap.description: Print: the first letter of a chapter's first paragraph as a three-line initial (default false). Skipped, with the text left as it is, when the paragraph does not start with a letter.

font.description: The body font. A DOCX names a font and the reader's machine supplies it. A PDF embeds one: Liberation Serif (the default; metric-compatible with Times New Roman) or Liberation Mono (Courier New); the other names fall back to Liberation Serif with a warning.

footnotes.description: Print: footnotes at the foot of the page they are on (page, the default), as endnotes at the end of each chapter (chapter), or all together after the last chapter (book).

format.description: The file: docx, epub, md (Markdown), pdf (print-ready, laid out by this program) or html-paged (one HTML file with CSS paged media, to print from a browser). odt, rtf, latex, rst and mediawiki are written by the Pandoc program from the compile Markdown, and only while an administrator has switched the Pandoc bridge on.

ghosts.description: Ghosted text: omit (the compile presets' default) leaves it out; keep prints it as ordinary text.

gutter_inches.description: Print: extra space added to the inside margin for the binding, 0 to 1.5 inches. Printers ask for more of it in a thicker book; the preview warns when the inside margin is under the commonly asked minimum for the page count.

header.description: The running header from page 2: 'Surname / Title / 12', 'Title / 12', or none.

header_title.description: The short title in the running header; default the title.

header_upper.description: Upper-case the title in the running header (Shunn's format does).

hyphenate.description: Print: break words at the end of a line (default false). Not built: setting it is refused until a hyphenation dictionary ships.

imprint.description: Print: the text of the copyright page, up to 8 lines and 600 characters. Default: 'Copyright © Name' and 'All rights reserved.', with no year (the program never reads the clock; put the year in this text).

indent_inches.description: First-line indent of a paragraph, 0 to 2 inches. The first paragraph after a heading or a scene break is never indented.

justify.description: Justify the body text (a book; never a manuscript).

language.description: Overrides the project's language tag (BCP 47), up to 16 characters.

link_urls.description: Write a link's address in parentheses after its text (default false). DOCX never carries a live link.

margin_bottom.description: Print: the bottom margin in inches, 0.25 to 3.

margin_inside.description: Print: the inside margin (the edge at the spine) in inches, 0.25 to 3, before the gutter is added.

margin_outside.description: Print: the outside margin (the edge away from the spine) in inches, 0.25 to 3.

margin_top.description: Print: the top margin in inches, 0.25 to 3 (default: margin_inches).

notes.description: Notes documents (the ones you keep for yourself): none (default), or appendix (after the back matter, under a Notes heading).

ornament.description: The text of an ornament scene break, up to 8 characters (default a centred asterism-like line of three dots).

own_cover.description: EPUB: use the project's own cover (project.cover_layout.get) when it has one. Default true; false puts the generated cover in its place. A release for a public Git remote follows that remote's include_cover.

page_numbers.description: Where page numbers go when the header is none or for a book: in the header, a centred footer, or nowhere.

page_size.description: The page (trim size for print): letter, a4, a5, or a trade size in inches (5x8, 5.25x8, 5.5x8.5, 6x9). DOCX supports every size too.

part_pages.description: A heading for each part (default true). false folds a part's own text into what follows and shows no part heading.

running_heads.description: Print: a running head on each page except chapter openers and blank pages: the author on left-hand pages, the title on right-hand pages (default true).

scene_break.description: A scene break is # (manuscript standard), * * * or the ornament text.

scene_titles.description: Print the titles of scenes as subheadings (default false: a scene is a break, not a heading).

space_after_pt.description: Space after a paragraph in points, 0 to 36.

the_end.description: 'THE END' after the last chapter (default false).

title_layout.description: manuscript: contact block top left, word count top right, title a third of the way down. book: title, subtitle and author centred.

toc.description: Print: a contents page after the front matter, with the page each part and chapter starts on (default true).

word_count.description: The title page's word count: 'about 80,000 words', 'Word count: 80,000' or none.

page_count.description: Use this page count instead of the layout's (2 to 1,500). Printers print leaves, so give an even number.

page_thickness_in.description: The paper's thickness per page in inches (0.0005 to 0.01), from your printer's cover template or guide. Required: the spine is the page count times this.

part.description: Which file: cover (the default) is the one page a printer takes, the whole wrap, named <title>-cover.pdf; front is the front alone at trim plus bleed (<title>-cover-front.pdf); proof is the proof page, the wrap at half size with the cut lines over it (<title>-cover-proof.pdf), for a cover with a layout, never for a printer. Each is recorded as its own export.

preset.description: A print preset (print-6x9, print-5x8, ...); its trim size and layout give the page count. Default print-6x9.

profile.description: The printer's figures for the text-safe margin, the barcode box and the page count from which the spine has type. Default generic. With no layout the cover keeps its own margin and barcode place unless a profile is named.

back.description: In points from the left edge of the wrap (bleed included).

barcode_box.description: The barcode box on the lower right of the back, in points from the left and bottom edges of the wrap.

layout.description: Present when the cover is made from the project's own layout.

measured_spine_in.description: A wrap's spine as measured from its picture.

pictures.description: Each placed picture and its resolution where it prints.

proof.description: The PDF has a third page, the proof.

stale.description: A wrap whose measured spine is over 1/32 in from the book's: cover_wrap_stale.

wrap_width_in.description: The first page's width: for a wrap, the picture's measured size, whatever the book's spine.

profile.description: The profile in force (generic by default).

spine_has_text.description: The spine carries type: it is a quarter inch or more, the book has the profile's pages, and the cover is not a wrap or right to left.

text_margin_in.description: Text and important art stay this far inside the trim (the profile's; a generated cover with no profile named keeps 0.125 in in its guides).

code.description: A stable token: chapter_untitled, front_matter_untitled, scene_break_at_end, scene_break_at_start, empty_document, not_compiled, notes_excluded, no_author, no_contact, image_missing, image_remote, image_skipped, nothing_to_compile; and from a PDF: missing_glyph, script_unsupported, font_substituted, loose_lines, overfull_line, widow_orphan, image_low_resolution, image_not_embedded, gutter_small, few_pages, layout_limit, table_columns, table_images, nesting_flattened, note_not_set, layout_refused; from a cover: spine_narrow, odd_page_count.

part.description: A cover warning only: which part of the cover it is about (the spine, the barcode's back, a wrap or a side). Empty for every other warning and for a cover warning about the cover as a whole.

wrap_width_in.description: Back, spine and front with bleed on both outer edges.

ops.name: compile.preview
ops.desc: Preview a compile without writing a file: the title page, the running header, the chapters with their words and estimated pages, the first pages as blocks, and warnings (an untitled chapter, a scene break at a chapter's end, documents skipped because they are marked do not compile, words in notes left out). For a DOCX the page numbers are an estimate (Word's own layout decides); for a PDF preset (print-6x9 and the others) the preview runs the same layout as the export, so the page count, the page each part starts on and the warnings are the file's, and it returns the page geometry and the first pages as placed lines. Writes nothing and records nothing; the response holds your contact block and the first pages of the text, so it is never kept for idempotent replay.

justify.description: Justify the body text (a book; never a manuscript).

language.description: Overrides the project's language tag (BCP 47), up to 16 characters.

link_urls.description: Write a link's address in parentheses after its text (default false). DOCX never carries a live link.

margin_bottom.description: Print: the bottom margin in inches, 0.25 to 3.

margin_outside.description: Print: the outside margin (the edge away from the spine) in inches, 0.25 to 3.

margin_top.description: Print: the top margin in inches, 0.25 to 3 (default: margin_inches).

notes.description: Notes documents (the ones you keep for yourself): none (default), or appendix (after the back matter, under a Notes heading).

ornament.description: The text of an ornament scene break, up to 8 characters (default a centred asterism-like line of three dots).

own_cover.description: EPUB: use the project's own cover (project.cover_layout.get) when it has one. Default true; false puts the generated cover in its place. A release for a public Git remote follows that remote's include_cover.

page_size.description: The page (trim size for print): letter, a4, a5, or a trade size in inches (5x8, 5.25x8, 5.5x8.5, 6x9). DOCX supports every size too.

the_end.description: 'THE END' after the last chapter (default false).

toc.description: Print: a contents page after the front matter, with the page each part and chapter starts on (default true).

ops.name: edition.diff
ops.desc: Compare the project as it stands with one of its editions, chapter by chapter, so a reviewer can step through what changed in a revised book. Each chapter of the edition is paired with its document (by what the import recorded, then by source path, then by title, then by the text they share), so renamed, moved, split, merged, added and removed chapters are found. Each step has a status (unchanged, edited, moved, split, merged, added, removed), word counts, words added and removed (never a net figure), and how it was paired: a method and a score, and guess=true for a pairing made by title or similarity, which is a heuristic and not a fact. Pass chapter (a step's key) to get that step's differences one at a time, paragraph by paragraph and word by word inside a reworded paragraph (the edition's text: editors, and a key with the write scope). A chapter that was left out of the project at import is shown only to editors. Two texts that share too little say too_different and are not diffed. Nothing is changed.

chapter.description: A step's key (from a previous answer): returns that step with its differences (hunks), one by one, each with the words that changed. The hunks carry the edition's text: this needs the editor role and, for a key, the write scope (as edition.download does). Without it the steps carry no hunks and readers can call it.

guess.description: The pairing is a heuristic (title, similarity, or a path between two editions): show it as a guess, not a fact.

method.description: What paired the chapters, from the surest: recorded (the import recorded it), path (the same source file), title, similarity (mostly the same text).

score.description: Confidence of the pairing, 0 to 1. 1 is what the import recorded; the others are guesses and their scores are only comparable with each other.

similarity.description: How much text the paired chapters share, 0 to 1 (runs of three words; sampled on a very large book).

moved.description: The chapter is somewhere else in the order or the tree (the status is moved only when its text is unchanged).

note.description: Why a step was not compared, or compared coarsely.

offer.description: Only for a comparison with the project: what can be done with this step.

confirm.description: Taking the chapter needs confirm_guess: it was paired with the edition's by a guess, not from the import's record.

reason.description: Why not, when neither is possible.

suggest.description: The differences can be offered as suggestions (one chapter, one document, paired one to one).

take.description: The chapter can be put back as it was in the edition (edition.take).

added.description: Words only the second text has.

removed.description: Words only the first text has.

too_different.description: The two texts have too little in common to compare chapter by chapter; no chapter was diffed.

ops.name: edition.download
ops.desc: Download the source file of an edition, byte for byte as it was imported (checked against its recorded SHA-256). Owners and editors only, and an API key needs the write scope, as for an export: it is the whole book as it was received.

ops.name: edition.get
ops.desc: One edition with its chapters: where each came from in the book (source_path), the document it became, and its size. The book's own text is not returned.

chapters.description: In reading order. Each says where it sits in the source (source_path), what it became (document_id) and how big it is; the text it was imported as is not returned.

document_id.description: The document it became. Empty when the writer left it out or the document is gone; several chapters can name one document (merged), and a chapter split into scenes names the chapter's document.

parent_ord.description: The ord of the part or chapter it sits in; 0 at the top.

sha256.description: Of the baseline Markdown (Baseline).

source_path.description: The file in the source, with #fragment when a file holds more than one chapter.

has_file.description: The source file is kept and can be downloaded by an editor or the owner.

identifier.description: The book's own identifier (an ISBN or urn:uuid), as the source states it.

imported_by.description: The person who imported it: shown to the project's owners and to administrators only.

label.description: What the edition is called: its title and date unless you named it.

metadata.description: What the source says about itself (title, authors, language, publisher, date) and counts of what the import read and did not keep.

sha256.description: Of the source file's bytes.

size.description: Bytes of the source file.

source_id.description: The import record (project_sources) this edition was made by.

ops.name: edition.list
ops.desc: The editions of a project: the books it was imported from, with each one's label, identifier, source file hash and size, and when it was imported. The source file itself is edition.download.

has_file.description: The source file is kept and can be downloaded by an editor or the owner.

identifier.description: The book's own identifier (an ISBN or urn:uuid), as the source states it.

imported_by.description: The person who imported it: shown to the project's owners and to administrators only.

label.description: What the edition is called: its title and date unless you named it.

metadata.description: What the source says about itself (title, authors, language, publisher, date) and counts of what the import read and did not keep.

sha256.description: Of the source file's bytes.

size.description: Bytes of the source file.

source_id.description: The import record (project_sources) this edition was made by.

ops.name: edition.suggest
ops.desc: Turn differences between a chapter and its edition into suggestions on the document, one suggestion for each difference, to be accepted or rejected one at a time in the review queue ("restore this passage from the source edition"). The same caps and refusals as suggestion.create: a difference whose text carries a link, a picture, a heading or a marker the document would not accept is skipped with its reason, and so is every difference of a chapter that was split or merged. base_revision must be current. The text is not changed until an editor accepts a suggestion; each one tells the project's owner and editors.

base_revision.description: The document's revision you read; it must be current (409 with current_revision otherwise).

chapter.description: The step's key (edition.diff). It must be a chapter paired one to one with a document, and edited.

edition_id.description: The edition the project is compared against.

hunks.description: Which differences (their ids from the step's hunks): each becomes a suggestion that puts the edition's text back (or, for a passage the edition does not have, removes it). Empty: all of them that can be offered, up to 20.

note.description: Added to the suggestions' note, up to 2,000 characters.

more.description: Differences that could be offered and were not, because a call makes at most 20: call again.

stopped.description: Why the call ended early (the project's open-suggestion cap, a save that came in); what was made stays made, and the rest is in skipped.

ops.name: edition.take
ops.desc: Take the edition's text for a whole chapter ("keep mine" is not calling this): the document's text becomes what the edition had, as a new version of the document. The text it replaces is kept first, with reason snapshot, and the new version has reason restore, so the history undoes it; no words are credited to the writer's goals. Only a chapter paired one to one (or merged into one document) is taken: a chapter that was split into several documents, added or removed is not. base_revision must be current. Use dry_run to see it first.

base_revision.description: The document's revision you read; it must be current.

confirm_guess.description: Needed when the step's offer says confirm: the chapter was paired with the edition's by a guess (title or similarity, or a merged step with one guessed member), not from what the import recorded.

edition_id.description: The edition the project is compared against.

revision.description: The document's revision now.

revision_id.description: The version written. The text before it was kept first, so restoring the version before this one undoes it.

unchanged.description: The document already had exactly the edition's text.

ops.name: entity.alias.add
ops.desc: Add an alias (a nickname, a title, a former name) to an entity. An alias another live entity in the Compendium already uses as a name or alias, or that is this entity's own name, is refused with a 409 that names it: a mention of that word would not say which entity it means. Editor.

alias.description: Up to 200 characters on one line.

notes.description: Where the alias comes from or who uses it, up to 1,000 characters.

fields.description: Custom field values by key, as canonical strings (a number as 34, a date as YYYY-MM-DD).

redirected_from.description: Set when the id you asked for was merged into this entity; use this entity's id from now on.

revision.description: Increments on every change to the sheet itself; send it back as base_revision to refuse a stale write.

sort_name.description: What lists sort by when it is not the name (a surname first). Empty means the name.

updated_at.description: Moves on any change, including aliases and relationships.

ops.name: entity.alias.remove
ops.desc: Remove one alias from an entity, by the alias id entity.get lists. Editor.

alias_id.description: The alias to remove, from entity.get.

fields.description: Custom field values by key, as canonical strings (a number as 34, a date as YYYY-MM-DD).

redirected_from.description: Set when the id you asked for was merged into this entity; use this entity's id from now on.

revision.description: Increments on every change to the sheet itself; send it back as base_revision to refuse a stale write.

sort_name.description: What lists sort by when it is not the name (a surname first). Empty means the name.

updated_at.description: Moves on any change, including aliases and relationships.

removed.description: False when the entity had no such alias.

ops.name: entity.appears_in
ops.desc: Which books mention this entity: for each project the caller can open, how many documents and mentions, and the first appearance. Projects the caller cannot open are counted in hidden_projects, never named. A key pinned to a Compendium sees counts only.

hidden_projects.description: Projects that mention it which the caller cannot open. Counted, never named.

first.description: The first manuscript document that mentions it, in reading order.

breadcrumb.description: Ancestors from the top of the tree, nearest last; empty at the top level.

indexing.description: A rescan is owed for this project; counts may be behind.

ops.name: entity.create
ops.desc: Create an entity (character, place, item, org or concept) in a Compendium, with a summary, a Markdown body, typed custom fields and aliases. The name is unique among the Compendium's live entities ignoring case and spacing, and no alias may equal another entity's name or alias; a clash is a 409 that names the other entity. Editor.

aliases.description: Other names, up to 100. An alias another live entity uses as a name or alias is refused.

fields.description: Custom field values by key. Each key must be defined for the kind (entity.field.set); an empty value leaves a field unset.

kind.description: Fixed once created.

name.description: Up to 200 characters. Unique among the Compendium's live entities, ignoring case and spacing, and not equal to anyone's alias.

sort_name.description: What lists sort by when it is not the name.

summary.description: One or two lines, up to 1,000 characters.

fields.description: Custom field values by key, as canonical strings (a number as 34, a date as YYYY-MM-DD).

redirected_from.description: Set when the id you asked for was merged into this entity; use this entity's id from now on.

revision.description: Increments on every change to the sheet itself; send it back as base_revision to refuse a stale write.

sort_name.description: What lists sort by when it is not the name (a surname first). Empty means the name.

updated_at.description: Moves on any change, including aliases and relationships.

ops.name: entity.field.list
ops.desc: List a Compendium's custom entity fields, by kind: key, label, type (text, number, date or choice) and the choices of a choice field. A new Compendium starts with a few starter fields (a character's role, age, appearance, voice, wants, fears, secrets and arc).

kind.description: Only one kind of entity.

choices.description: The allowed values of a choice field; empty for the other types.

key.description: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores; starts with a letter. Entities store values under it.

ops.name: entity.field.remove
ops.desc: Remove a custom field definition. Refused while entities or project overrides hold a value for it, unless drop_values is set, which deletes those values too. Editor.

drop_values.description: Also delete the values entities hold under this key. Without it, a field that is in use is refused.

key.description: The field's key.

kind.description: The entity kind.

overrides_dropped.description: Project overrides that held a value, which was deleted.

removed.description: False when there was no such field.

values_dropped.description: Entities that held a value, which was deleted.

ops.name: entity.field.set
ops.desc: Define a custom field for one kind of entity, or change an existing one's label and choices (its type is fixed once defined). Entities can only hold values for fields defined here. Editor.

choices.description: Required for choice fields: the allowed values, up to 50. Removing a value that entities use is refused.

key.description: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores; starts with a letter; up to 32 characters.

label.description: What the field is called on a sheet. Defaults to the key.

type.description: Fixed once values exist: remove the field to change it.

choices.description: The allowed values of a choice field; empty for the other types.

key.description: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores; starts with a letter. Entities store values under it.

ops.name: entity.first_appearance
ops.desc: The first document, in reading order, that mentions an entity, per project (a Compendium is shared, so first appearance is a fact about one book). With entity it answers for that one; without it, for every entity the caller may read, each with the document or null, and how many documents and mentions it has. Manuscript text only unless all=true.

all.description: Count notes and front and back matter too.

entity.description: One entity (an id, a name or an alias); without it, every entity the caller may read.

hidden.description: The project reaches entities the caller may not read; they are left out and not counted.

indexing.description: A rescan is owed; the answers may be behind.

document.description: The first document in reading order that mentions it; absent when none does.

breadcrumb.description: Ancestors from the top of the tree, nearest last; empty at the top level.

documents.description: How many documents mention it.

name.description: The effective name: the book's override, else the Compendium's.

ops.name: entity.get
ops.desc: Get one entity sheet with its aliases, custom fields and relationships. An id that was merged into another entity answers with the target and redirected_from, for a year.

id.description: Entity id. An id that was merged into another entity still answers, with redirected_from set, for a year.

fields.description: Custom field values by key, as canonical strings (a number as 34, a date as YYYY-MM-DD).

redirected_from.description: Set when the id you asked for was merged into this entity; use this entity's id from now on.

revision.description: Increments on every change to the sheet itself; send it back as base_revision to refuse a stale write.

sort_name.description: What lists sort by when it is not the name (a surname first). Empty means the name.

updated_at.description: Moves on any change, including aliases and relationships.

relations.description: Relationships with live entities, up to 500.

direction.description: out: this entity is the source; in: it is the target; both: a symmetric relationship.

label.description: How the relationship reads from this entity: "mother of" on the source, the inverse label on the target.

ops.name: entity.list
ops.desc: List a Compendium's entities in sort order, a page at a time, without bodies. Filter by kind, by q (names and aliases containing it) or by name (the entity called exactly this, by name or alias: how to turn a name into an id). Trashed ones with state=trashed.

kind.description: Only one kind.

name.description: The entity whose name or alias is exactly this, ignoring case and spacing: the way to turn a name into an id.

q.description: Names and aliases containing these characters, ignoring case.

state.description: live (default), trashed or all.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; absent on the last.

total.description: Every entity matching the filters, not just this page.

ops.name: entity.merge
ops.desc: Merge this entity (the source) into another of the same kind in the same Compendium (into_id). With dry_run it writes nothing and returns the plan: aliases moved, dropped and blocked, fields copied and in conflict, relationships rewired or dropped, overrides and links moved, scenes repointed. The real merge applies that same plan in one transaction, deletes the source, and leaves a redirect from its old id to the target for a year. Where both entities hold a different value for a custom field, field_choices must say source or target for each (and override:<project id> where a project overrode both); an unresolved conflict refuses the merge. Editor.

body.description: Which body survives, or append the source's below the target's. Default target.

field_choices.description: Per conflicting custom field key, source or target; override:<project id> for a project that overrode both.

id.description: The source entity: it is deleted by the merge.

name_as_alias.description: Keep the source's name as an alias of the target. Default true.

item.description: The target after a real merge.

fields.description: Custom field values by key, as canonical strings (a number as 34, a date as YYYY-MM-DD).

redirected_from.description: Set when the id you asked for was merged into this entity; use this entity's id from now on.

revision.description: Increments on every change to the sheet itself; send it back as base_revision to refuse a stale write.

sort_name.description: What lists sort by when it is not the name (a surname first). Empty means the name.

updated_at.description: Moves on any change, including aliases and relationships.

merged.description: True once the merge has been applied.

aliases_blocked.description: Aliases of the source a third entity uses: dropped.

aliases_duplicate.description: Aliases of the source the target already has (or is named): dropped.

extra.description: Rows other features move with the merge, by feature.

choice.description: What the request chose: source or target; empty while unresolved.

fields_taken.description: Custom fields only the source had: copied to the target.

hidden_override_conflicts.description: Projects the caller cannot open that overrode both entities. They are not named and cannot be chosen for: the target's override is kept there.

links_dropped.description: Project links the target already had.

locked_override_conflicts.description: Projects the caller is on but has not unlocked (they have a passphrase) that overrode both entities. A real merge is refused while this is not zero: their source override would be deleted without anyone being able to see or choose it. Unlock them, then choose per project.

name_as_alias.description: The source's name, kept as an alias of the target; empty when not.

key.description: The field_choices key to answer with: override:<project id>.

overrides_dropped.description: Source overrides discarded: the request chose the target's, or the project is one the caller cannot open.

redirects_repointed.description: Older merged ids that now lead to the target.

reason.description: self: it would relate the target to itself. duplicate: the target already has the same relationship.

scene_refs_repointed.description: Scenes whose point of view or location was the source.

unresolved.description: field_choices keys still needing an answer. A real merge is refused while this is not empty.

ops.name: entity.referenced.list
ops.desc: The entities of the Compendiums this one references, read-only, in sort order, a page at a time. Only entities of Compendiums the caller is a member of are returned (hidden says some were left out); being able to read this Compendium does not open the ones it references. Each entity says which Compendium it lives in and whether the caller could edit it there (editable); to change one, use entity.update in that Compendium.

kind.description: Only one kind.

q.description: Names and aliases containing these characters, ignoring case.

hidden.description: True when a referenced Compendium has entities the caller may not see. They are neither counted nor named.

editable.description: The caller is an editor of the Compendium it lives in. Never editable through the reference.

ops.name: entity.relation.add
ops.desc: Relate this entity to another in the same Compendium with a typed edge (family, ally, rival, mentor, romantic, member or custom) and a label that reads from this side ("mother of"). inverse_label is how it reads from the other side ("daughter of"); a symmetric edge reads the same both ways. The same edge twice is a 409. Editor.

id.description: The entity the relationship reads from (the source).

inverse_label.description: How it reads from the other side, e.g. "daughter of".

kind.description: Default custom.

label.description: How it reads from the source, e.g. "mother of". Required for custom; defaults to the kind.

notes.description: Up to 1,000 characters.

symmetric.description: The same both ways (siblings, rivals): the inverse label is not used.

to_entity_id.description: The other entity, in the same Compendium.

direction.description: out: this entity is the source; in: it is the target; both: a symmetric relationship.

label.description: How the relationship reads from this entity: "mother of" on the source, the inverse label on the target.

ops.name: entity.relation.list
ops.desc: List an entity's relationships with live entities, as they read from this entity: direction out, in or both, and the label for that side. Up to 500.

direction.description: out: this entity is the source; in: it is the target; both: a symmetric relationship.

label.description: How the relationship reads from this entity: "mother of" on the source, the inverse label on the target.

ops.name: entity.relation.remove
ops.desc: Remove a relationship that touches this entity, by the relation id entity.relation.list gives. Editor.

id.description: Entity id; the relationship must touch it.

removed.description: False when this entity had no such relationship.

ops.name: entity.restore
ops.desc: Take an entity out of the trash. Refused with a 409 naming the other entity if its name or an alias has been used since. Editor.

fields.description: Custom field values by key, as canonical strings (a number as 34, a date as YYYY-MM-DD).

redirected_from.description: Set when the id you asked for was merged into this entity; use this entity's id from now on.

revision.description: Increments on every change to the sheet itself; send it back as base_revision to refuse a stale write.

sort_name.description: What lists sort by when it is not the name (a surname first). Empty means the name.

updated_at.description: Moves on any change, including aliases and relationships.

ops.name: entity.trash
ops.desc: Move an entity to the trash: it leaves lists, search, projects and the mirror, and its name and aliases are free to reuse. Nothing is deleted. Editor.

fields.description: Custom field values by key, as canonical strings (a number as 34, a date as YYYY-MM-DD).

redirected_from.description: Set when the id you asked for was merged into this entity; use this entity's id from now on.

revision.description: Increments on every change to the sheet itself; send it back as base_revision to refuse a stale write.

sort_name.description: What lists sort by when it is not the name (a surname first). Empty means the name.

updated_at.description: Moves on any change, including aliases and relationships.

ops.name: entity.update
ops.desc: Change an entity's name, sort name, summary, body, colour or custom field values. Send only what changes. The kind is fixed. Pass base_revision to refuse a stale write. Editor.

base_revision.description: The revision you last saw; a different current revision is refused with 409 and the current one.

fields.description: Custom field values to set by key; the rest stay. An empty value clears that field.
Custom field values by key, as canonical strings (a number as 34, a date as YYYY-MM-DD).

redirected_from.description: Set when the id you asked for was merged into this entity; use this entity's id from now on.

revision.description: Increments on every change to the sheet itself; send it back as base_revision to refuse a stale write.

sort_name.description: What lists sort by when it is not the name (a surname first). Empty means the name.

updated_at.description: Moves on any change, including aliases and relationships.

ops.name: export.compile
ops.desc: Compile the manuscript with a preset into a DOCX (US Standard Manuscript, UK manuscript, styled), an EPUB 3 (also, in a custom preset's format option, an odt, rtf, latex, rst or mediawiki file written by the Pandoc program from the compile Markdown, only while an administrator has the Pandoc bridge on; the Pandoc version is in the export's record and input hash, and the same text gives the same file only with the same version), plain Markdown, a print-ready PDF (print-6x9 and the other print and proof presets: fonts embedded, mirrored margins, running heads, roman and arabic page numbers, contents, footnotes at the foot of the page, a deterministic file that is the same for the same input hash) or one paged HTML file to print from a browser. Documents marked do not compile, notes, private notes, ghosted text and alternatives comments are left out. Deterministic, recorded with a manifest of the documents and hashes and the preset; run compile.preview first.

options.description: Options that override the preset for this compile only.

back_cover.description: EPUB: put the project's own back cover (project.cover_layout.get) last in the book, on a page of its own outside the reading order (default false). Only a layout that gives the back a picture, or a wrap, has one; the generated cover has no back page. Off when own_cover is false.

byline.description: The name on the title page, when it is not the project's author name (a pen name).

chapter_drop.description: How far down the page a chapter title starts, in inches, 0 to 5.

chapter_heading.description: What a chapter heading says: 'Chapter 3: Title', 'Chapter 3', the title alone, or nothing.

chapter_label.description: The word before a chapter number (default Chapter), up to 24 characters.

chapter_ornament.description: Print: the ornament under a chapter heading (default false). The ornament is the scene-break ornament.

chapter_start.description: Each chapter starts a new page, or (recto, PDF) on the next right-hand page with a blank page inserted when needed, or runs on.

clear.description: Options to reset to empty when this is laid over a preset: byline, header_title, ornament, language, chapter_label, imprint. An empty string in a field means 'not set', so this is how to clear one.

contact.description: DOCX manuscript title page: show your contact block (default true). false leaves the block off the page and leaves the word count top right.

copyright_page.description: Print: a copyright page after the title page (default true).

cover.description: EPUB: put the cover first: a cover page and the cover image the shops and readers use. It is the project's own cover when it has one (project.cover_layout.get), else the generated cover. Default true. KDP takes the cover as a separate upload and asks for no cover page in the file, so turn this off for a file bound for KDP.

cover_page.description: Print, for a proof or a copy you print yourself (default false): the cover's front as the first page of the PDF, edge to edge (into the bleed with crop marks), followed by a blank page so the title page stays a right-hand page. Do not upload a file made with it to a print-on-demand printer as the interior: KDP and IngramSpark take the cover as a separate file, and a printer counts and prints every page of the interior, so these two pages would be printed and would change the page count and the spine. The page count that export.cover and compile.cover_spec use does not include them. It is the project's own cover, or the generated one when there is none or own_cover is false. A right-to-left book has no PDF.

crop_marks.description: Print: a proof with crop marks: the page grows by a 0.125 inch bleed and a quarter-inch slug, the marks are drawn outside the trim and the trim and bleed boxes are set (default false).

drop_cap.description: Print: the first letter of a chapter's first paragraph as a three-line initial (default false). Skipped, with the text left as it is, when the paragraph does not start with a letter.

font.description: The body font. A DOCX names a font and the reader's machine supplies it. A PDF embeds one: Liberation Serif (the default; metric-compatible with Times New Roman) or Liberation Mono (Courier New); the other names fall back to Liberation Serif with a warning.

footnotes.description: Print: footnotes at the foot of the page they are on (page, the default), as endnotes at the end of each chapter (chapter), or all together after the last chapter (book).

format.description: The file: docx, epub, md (Markdown), pdf (print-ready, laid out by this program) or html-paged (one HTML file with CSS paged media, to print from a browser). odt, rtf, latex, rst and mediawiki are written by the Pandoc program from the compile Markdown, and only while an administrator has switched the Pandoc bridge on.

ghosts.description: Ghosted text: omit (the compile presets' default) leaves it out; keep prints it as ordinary text.

gutter_inches.description: Print: extra space added to the inside margin for the binding, 0 to 1.5 inches. Printers ask for more of it in a thicker book; the preview warns when the inside margin is under the commonly asked minimum for the page count.

header.description: The running header from page 2: 'Surname / Title / 12', 'Title / 12', or none.

header_title.description: The short title in the running header; default the title.

header_upper.description: Upper-case the title in the running header (Shunn's format does).

hyphenate.description: Print: break words at the end of a line (default false). Not built: setting it is refused until a hyphenation dictionary ships.

imprint.description: Print: the text of the copyright page, up to 8 lines and 600 characters. Default: 'Copyright © Name' and 'All rights reserved.', with no year (the program never reads the clock; put the year in this text).

indent_inches.description: First-line indent of a paragraph, 0 to 2 inches. The first paragraph after a heading or a scene break is never indented.

justify.description: Justify the body text (a book; never a manuscript).

language.description: Overrides the project's language tag (BCP 47), up to 16 characters.

link_urls.description: Write a link's address in parentheses after its text (default false). DOCX never carries a live link.

margin_bottom.description: Print: the bottom margin in inches, 0.25 to 3.

margin_inside.description: Print: the inside margin (the edge at the spine) in inches, 0.25 to 3, before the gutter is added.

margin_outside.description: Print: the outside margin (the edge away from the spine) in inches, 0.25 to 3.

margin_top.description: Print: the top margin in inches, 0.25 to 3 (default: margin_inches).

notes.description: Notes documents (the ones you keep for yourself): none (default), or appendix (after the back matter, under a Notes heading).

ornament.description: The text of an ornament scene break, up to 8 characters (default a centred asterism-like line of three dots).

own_cover.description: EPUB: use the project's own cover (project.cover_layout.get) when it has one. Default true; false puts the generated cover in its place. A release for a public Git remote follows that remote's include_cover.

page_numbers.description: Where page numbers go when the header is none or for a book: in the header, a centred footer, or nowhere.

page_size.description: The page (trim size for print): letter, a4, a5, or a trade size in inches (5x8, 5.25x8, 5.5x8.5, 6x9). DOCX supports every size too.

part_pages.description: A heading for each part (default true). false folds a part's own text into what follows and shows no part heading.

ops.name: export.cover
ops.desc: A print cover as a PDF. The default file is exactly one page, the full wrap with bleed, which is what KDP and IngramSpark take (part front is the front on its own, part proof the proof). With no cover layout (or own_cover false) it is the generated cover: a flat colour from the project's cover colour with white type, no gradient and no image, in any language. With the project's own layout (project.cover_layout.get) it is made from the layout: an image side fills its panel to the bleed, cropped from the centre, a page side lays its picture on a page of the trim by its fit, scale, position, background and margin, a generated side keeps the typographic drawing, a back left out is the cover colour, and a wrap picture is the whole first page at its measured size with nothing drawn over it; part proof is a separate file, the proof (the wrap at half size with the trim, bleed, spine folds, text-safe margin and barcode box over it, and a legend: never send it to a printer), and part front the front alone. The layout's trim must be the preset's (cover_trim_mismatch refuses otherwise). Pictures go in at full resolution (a JPEG as it is), in RGB: a picture's own RGB colour profile goes with it, anything else is DeviceRGB, and a printer that wants CMYK converts. profile (kdp, ingram, generic) sets the text-safe margin, barcode box and the page count from which the spine carries type. The spine is set only when it is wide enough for type and the book has the profile's pages. Warnings: image_low_resolution (under 285 dpi where the picture prints; print asks for 300, and a picture made at 300 for the trim lands at about 288 once it covers the bleed), cover_print_cropped (an image side loses over 5 per cent of its picture to fill the panel and bleed), cover_wrap_stale (the wrap's spine is over 1/32 in from the book's), cover_margin_crossed, cover_bleed_missing, cover_barcode_area, spine_narrow, spine_few_pages, spine_rtl, cover_profile_not_srgb. Optional guides (trim, spine and safe-area lines) and a white box for the barcode. A right-to-left book needs page_count; its layout may not have a generated side (cover_rtl_text refuses the file, compile.cover_spec still measures it). Deterministic and recorded. Check it against your printer's template.

ops.name: git.remote.create
ops.desc: Owner only. Add a push-only Git remote to a project (up to five per project; a private remote at an address that was ever public needs confirm_name, the new remote's name). For an ssh address a deploy key is generated; its public half is in the result to add at the host with write access, then scan and accept the host key. For https send the token, which is stored encrypted and never returned. Needs the server's secret key.

audience.description: public (the default, the strictest): only what a reader of the book sees: no notes, no do-not-compile documents, no ghosted text, no alternatives, no private notes, no outline details. private: the full mirror, for a backup in a repository only you can read.

confirm_name.description: Needed for a private remote at an address that was ever public, and for a public remote with include_cover on: the new remote's name, typed exactly. Refused with 409 confirmation_required (data.git_code) without it.

include_cover.description: Push the project's own cover too (the cover layout and its pictures). Default true for a private remote, false for a public one: carrying it to a public remote lets more reach a repository people can read, so it needs a person at a browser and confirm_name.

include_notes.description: Push the project's notes too. Default true for a private remote; a public remote never carries notes.

name.description: What the remote is for, like Backup. Also the deploy key's name.

confirm_name.description: Needed when the change lets more reach a repository that is, or may be, public: a public remote made private (the whole copy), only_done taken off, notes or the cover switched on, or the address changed on such a remote or to an address that was ever public. include_cover.description: Push the project's own cover (the layout and its pictures). acknowledged.description: Findings of the pre-push check the owner acknowledged, each for one file with one content.
