ops.name: git.signing.generate
ops.desc: Owner only. Generate the project's ed25519 signing key (the private half is stored encrypted and never returned), or replace it with replace=true. A remote signs its commits only when sign_commits is on. Needs the server's secret key.

replace.description: Required when the project already has a key: commits signed with the old key no longer verify against the new allowed-signers line.

exists.description: The project has a signing key.

allowed_signers.description: A line for an allowed-signers file (git config gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile) so that git verify-commit accepts the project's commits. The principal is * : any author email.

fingerprint.description: SHA256:... as ssh-keygen shows it.

public_key.description: An authorized_keys line. Add it at the host as a signing key (GitHub: Settings, SSH and GPG keys, key type Signing key).

ops.name: git.signing.get
ops.desc: The project's commit-signing key: its public half, fingerprint and an allowed-signers line. Owner only. The private half is never returned.

exists.description: The project has a signing key.

allowed_signers.description: A line for an allowed-signers file (git config gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile) so that git verify-commit accepts the project's commits. The principal is * : any author email.

public_key.description: An authorized_keys line. Add it at the host as a signing key (GitHub: Settings, SSH and GPG keys, key type Signing key).

ops.desc: Owner only. Remove a remote's trigger and its waiting deliveries.

remote_id.description: The remote. Optional while the project has exactly one.

ops.desc: A remote's push trigger: where it calls (scheme, host and port), whether it is on, the last delivery's short status. Owner only. The secret and the path are never returned.

ops.desc: Owner only. Set a remote's trigger: after every successful push one signed POST goes to the address, with the repository, the branch, the commit id and the project slug, and nothing of the manuscript. A new trigger gets a signing secret, shown once in the answer (as is a rotated one); the address's path is stored encrypted. Retried with backoff up to 5 attempts.

remote_id.description: The remote. Optional while the project has exactly one.

rotate_secret.description: Make a new signing secret; the answer shows it once.

url.description: https address to call (http only for the local network, where the administrator allowed it). Required to create the trigger.

last_status.description: A short line about the last delivery, never a response body.

origin.description: The address's scheme, host and port. Its path and query are stored encrypted and not shown.

pending.description: Deliveries waiting for a retry.

secret_hint.description: The start of the signing secret, to tell two apart. The secret itself is shown once, when it is made or rotated.

secret.description: The signing secret: shown only in the answer that made or rotated it. A receiver checks each delivery's Scriobh-Webhook-Signature with it (the webhook scheme: HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp, a full stop and the body).

ops.name: git.trigger.test
ops.desc: Owner only. Send one test delivery (event git.ping, no commit) to the trigger's address, signed as a real one, and say how it went in one short line. Not retried.

remote_id.description: The remote. Optional while the project has exactly one.

status.description: A short line, never a response body.

ops.name: goal.delete
ops.desc: Remove one of the caller's own goals (kind=daily or kind=project). Days already met stay met.

kind.description: daily or project.

ops.name: goal.list
ops.desc: List the caller's own goals on a project, with the project's shared word goal and deadline.

items.description: The caller's own goals on this project: at most one daily and one project goal.

end_date.description: Last local date the goal applies, or empty.

start_date.description: The local date the goal was set.

project_deadline.description: The project's shared deadline, YYYY-MM-DD, or empty.

project_word_goal.description: The project's shared word goal (project.update), 0 for none.

ops.name: goal.set
ops.desc: Set one of the caller's own goals on a project: a daily words-added target, or a total-word target with an optional deadline. Replaces the caller's goal of that kind. Goals count words added; cutting never counts against them.

end_date.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD. For a project goal, the deadline; for a daily goal, the last day it applies.

kind.description: daily: words added per day. project: the caller's own total-word target for the whole project (the shared target is set with project.update).

target_words.description: Words. Daily up to 100,000; project up to 10,000,000.

end_date.description: Last local date the goal applies, or empty.

start_date.description: The local date the goal was set.

ops.name: import.append
ops.desc: Add a previewed folder, document, book or export to an existing project as new documents after what is already there (and research notes after the research there), in one transaction. Existing documents are never changed. An EPUB is kept as an edition of the project.

docx.description: The same .docx that was previewed, base64.

docx_changes.description: With docx: what tracked changes become. suggest (default) imports the text as its author left it, every change rejected, and proposes each change inside a paragraph as a pending suggestion by its Word author (a label, not an account) at the time Word recorded; accepting them all in review gives the reviewers' text. Changes that cannot be suggestions (a whole paragraph inserted or deleted, a heading, a table, a footnote, code, over the caps of 300 per document and 1,000 per import, or ones the review checks would refuse) are taken as the reviewer left them, and the preview counts each kind. accept imports the final view and reject the original, with no suggestions. Word comments are imported as comments by their Word authors in every mode.

edition_label.description: With epub: what the edition is called (default: the preview's epub.label).

key.description: The node's key from the preview.

kind.description: Change what kind of document it is.

merge_into.description: Add this document's text to the end of the document with this key and remove this one; what was inside it goes into the other. Use with nothing else on the same edit. Footnotes are renumbered.

parent.description: Move this document, and what is inside it, to the end of the document with this key (or to the top level with an empty string). A document cannot be moved into itself or into what is inside it, and the tree stays at most ten levels deep.

skip.description: Leave this node, and everything inside it, out of the import.

split.description: Split this one file at its second-level headings (true) or keep it whole (false), whatever split_scenes says.

title.description: Rename the document.

epub.description: Instead of files, a zip or a Word document: an EPUB 2 or 3 book (.epub), base64. The reading order, metadata, cover, pictures and footnotes are read and the preview proposes parts, chapters and front and back matter, which the edits can rename, merge (merge_into), move (parent), skip and reorder. A book with DRM, or with a fixed layout, is refused. The file is kept intact, with its SHA-256, as an edition of the project (edition.list).

epub_pages.description: With epub: skip (default) leaves out the cover page and the title page, which the project's own title and author replace; keep imports a title page as front matter. The contents page is always left out.

epub_sections.description: With epub: how the text is cut into sections: toc (the book's table of contents), files (one for each file of its reading order), headings (at the chapter-level heading, for one long file), auto (default: toc, else files, else headings). The preview's epub.strategy says which was used.

content.description: The file as UTF-8 text; use data for anything that might not be.

path.description: Path relative to the folder, with forward slashes.

size.description: Size in bytes of a file whose bytes are not sent; -1 marks something that is not a regular file.

ghost_status.description: With a Ghost export: published (default) imports published posts and pages only; all adds drafts, scheduled and sent ones, which are marked do not compile.

ghost_types.description: With a Ghost export: posts (default), pages, or both.

pandoc.description: The same file that was previewed, base64 (with pandoc_format).

parent_id.description: Folder to add into; empty for the end of the top level.

pdf.description: Instead of files, a zip or a .docx: a PDF with a text layer, base64 (up to 32 MiB). The text is read, with its chapters taken from the outline or from headings; running heads, page numbers and a table of contents are removed, footnotes are kept, and the preview says what could not be recovered (scanned pages, tables, pictures, columns, right-to-left text) with a confidence for each page. A scanned or encrypted PDF is refused; nothing in a PDF is run.

pictures.description: With a Scrivener project, or a WordPress or Ghost export sent as a zip with its images folder: import (default) stores the pictures that are in what was sent as attachments of the project, checked and cleaned of their location, camera and other details, and links the text to them; skip leaves them out (each is marked [image]). A picture is never fetched from an address.

keys.description: The parent's children in the order wanted. Children you leave out follow, in their proposed order.

parent.description: Key of the parent node, or empty for the top level.

scrivener_notes.description: With a Scrivener project: private (default) puts each document's notes after its text as private notes; skip leaves them out.

scrivener_research.description: With a Scrivener project: notes (default) imports the Research folder as research notes (a picture becomes a note showing it, with pictures: import; PDFs and web pages are named in a note, not imported); skip leaves Research out.

scrivener_sheets.description: With a Scrivener project: notes (default) imports the Characters and Places folders as research notes; entities makes each character and place sheet an entity of the project's primary Compendium (a new project gets one, owned by you; adding to a project uses its primary Compendium if you may edit it). A name the Compendium already has, or a sheet with a picture, stays a research note, and the result says so.

token.description: The token import.append_preview returned for these same files.

wp_status.description: With a WordPress export: published (default) imports published posts and pages only; all adds drafts, pending, scheduled and private ones, which are marked do not compile.

wp_types.description: With a WordPress export: posts (default), pages, or both (pages go in a part called Pages after the posts).

comments.description: Comments written from a Word file's comments.

compendium_id.description: The primary Compendium made for the new project to hold those entities.

cover_used.description: With use_cover: the book's cover picture is now the project's own cover (project.cover_layout.get).

edition_id.description: With an EPUB: the edition recorded for the book (edition.get), whose source file is kept.

entities.description: Character and place sheets made entities (scrivener_sheets: entities).

pictures.description: Pictures stored as attachments of the project (or found there already, with the same bytes).

slug.description: The new project's slug; empty when importing into an existing project.

source_id.description: The recorded source (project_sources) of these documents.

suggestions.description: Pending suggestions written from a Word file's tracked changes.

contributors.description: Translators, editors, illustrators: named, not made authors.

kept.description: The cover is stored as an attachment of the project (it is not a document).

reason.description: Why it was not kept.

use_reason.description: Why the picture cannot be the project's own cover.

files.description: The book's files in reading order, each with the document its text became (key), or why it is not imported. The first 5,000.

key.description: The key of the proposed document that holds the text this file starts or continues; empty when the file is not imported.

notes.description: Footnotes taken out of the file.

path.description: Path inside the EPUB.

skipped.description: Why the file is not imported.

title.description: What the file's first heading says.

words.description: An estimate from the size of its text.

footnotes.description: Footnotes found and written as Markdown footnotes.

generator.description: The program that made the book, when it says.

identifier.description: The book's own identifier (an ISBN or urn:uuid) as it states it.

ops.name: import.apply
ops.desc: Create a new project from a previewed folder, document, book or export, with the writer's edits, in one transaction: all of it or none (documents, research notes, pictures as attachments, entities when asked, links, search). An EPUB is also kept, intact and hashed, as an edition of the project (edition.list). Send the same files and options and the preview's token.

docx.description: The same .docx that was previewed, base64.

docx_changes.description: With docx: what tracked changes become. suggest (default) imports the text as its author left it, every change rejected, and proposes each change inside a paragraph as a pending suggestion by its Word author (a label, not an account) at the time Word recorded; accepting them all in review gives the reviewers' text. Changes that cannot be suggestions (a whole paragraph inserted or deleted, a heading, a table, a footnote, code, over the caps of 300 per document and 1,000 per import, or ones the review checks would refuse) are taken as the reviewer left them, and the preview counts each kind. accept imports the final view and reject the original, with no suggestions. Word comments are imported as comments by their Word authors in every mode.

edition_label.description: With epub: what the edition is called (default: the preview's epub.label, the title and year).

edits.description: Renames, kind changes, skips, merges, moves and per-file splits, by node key.

kind.description: Change what kind of document it is.

epub.description: Instead of files, a zip or a Word document: an EPUB 2 or 3 book (.epub), base64. ops.name: presence.beat
ops.desc: Say that you have this project open (and optionally which document) and learn who else is here. The page sends it every 20 seconds while it is open and visible; a person is shown for 60 seconds after their last beat. Only for a person who has switched presence.share on (it is off for a new account): when it is off nothing is recorded and the answer says so, because sharing is symmetric: no one sees you and you see no one. Nothing is stored: the table is in memory, never in the database, a backup, an export or an event. No typing, cursor or text is ever sent. A reader sees no one; a reviewer sees who is here; an owner or an editor also sees which document. Browser session only. It does not count as activity for the session's or a protected project's idle limit.

ops.name: project.cover_layout.upload
ops.desc: Upload a cover picture. The request body is the picture itself (the CLI: --file @path); part says which part of the cover it is for: front, back or wrap. A PNG or a JPEG is accepted and cleaned (no EXIF, no GPS, no thumbnail) into a project attachment that a layout may then name; the answer is its id, size, resolution at the trim and any warnings. A wrap is measured at once (the resolution from its height, the spine from its width) and refused when it is not a wrap for the trim: under 150 dpi, or a spine under zero or over 2.5 in. CMYK JPEGs, SVG, GIF, WebP, a picture over 24 megapixels, a progressive JPEG too large to decode within the server's memory budget (save a baseline JPEG) and a PNG over 16 megapixels (send a JPEG) are refused with a sentence that says why. It cannot be previewed with --dry-run: it writes a file.

bleed_in.description: A wrap's bleed in inches (0 to 0.5), for measuring it. Default 0.125, or the layout's.

filename.description: A name for the picture, for display.

part.description: Which part of the cover the picture is for. A wrap is measured at once.

trim.description: The trim the cover is made for, to give the resolution and measure a wrap against: 6x9 (default, or the layout's), 5.5x8.5, 5.25x8, 5x8, a5, letter or a4.

attachment_id.description: Name this in a layout's front, back or wrap.

ops.name: project.member.add

An address nobody can be added under (unknown, removed, an API-only account, or an instance reader being made an editor) all answer the same way, so this cannot be used to list who is here. The project's Compendium is a separate door: add_to_compendium asks to add them to the primary Compendium too. It defaults to true for an editor and false for a reviewer or reader, and the result's compendium object says what was granted and, if nothing, why. Nothing is granted silently, and only the Compendium's owner can grant. Owner only.

ops.name: repo.account.connect
ops.desc: Connect your account at GitHub or a Forgejo or Gitea host with a personal access token. The token is checked with the host (one request to its API), stored encrypted, bound to that host, and never returned. It is yours: no one else, an administrator included, can use it. For a browser session only. Needs the server's secret key.

host.description: github.com by default for GitHub (or a GitHub Enterprise Server host); required for Forgejo: the host, like git.example.org or git.example.org:3000, without https://.

label.description: A name for the account in lists.

provider.description: github, or forgejo (Gitea speaks the same API).

token.description: A personal access token. GitHub: a fine-grained token with Administration (to create) and Contents (to push) on the repositories, or a classic one with repo. Forgejo and Gitea: an access token with repository write. Write-only: stored encrypted, never returned.

host.description: The web host: github.com, or your Forgejo or Gitea host.

login.description: The account the token belongs to, as the host reported it.

ops.name: repo.account.disconnect
ops.desc: Forget a connected account and its stored token. Remotes made with it keep their own copy of the token and are not touched. For a browser session only.

ops.name: repo.account.list
ops.desc: Your connected accounts at code hosts (GitHub, Forgejo, Gitea): host and login, never the token. For a browser session only.

host.description: The web host: github.com, or your Forgejo or Gitea host.

login.description: The account the token belongs to, as the host reported it.

ops.name: repo.list
ops.desc: The repositories your connected account can write to, one page of up to 50 from the host. A POST because it makes a request to the host with your token, which a project in the trash may not. Owner only, browser session only.

page.description: The host's page, from 1. A page holds up to 50 repositories.

q.description: Keep only repositories whose name contains this.

host.description: The web host: github.com, or your Forgejo or Gitea host.

login.description: The account the token belongs to, as the host reported it.

empty.description: The host says it has no content. repo.plan checks for sure.

next_page.description: Pass as page for the next one.

ops.name: repo.plan
ops.desc: A dry run of publishing the project to a repository: what will be created, the visibility, which files the first push holds (count, size, paths), which documents a public remote withholds and why, anything that looks like a secret, and whether a public repository needs the name typed. Reads from the host (does the repository exist, is it empty); changes nothing, there or here. Returns the plan_token repo.publish needs. Owner only, browser session only.

audience.description: public (the default, the strictest): only what a reader of the book sees. private: the full mirror; refused for a public repository.

description.description: For a new repository, up to 350 characters.

include_cover.description: Public audience: push the project's own cover (the layout and its pictures) too; the plan lists its files. A private audience always carries it.

include_notes.description: Private audience only: push the project's notes too.

mode.description: create (the default) makes a new repository and refuses a name that exists; existing takes a repository that is empty.

name.description: The repository's name.

only_done.description: Public audience: only documents whose status is done.

owner.description: The user or organization the repository belongs to. Default: the account itself.

path_prefix.description: Place the files in this subdirectory of the repository.

push_mode.description: How the remote pushes after the first push. Default manual.

sign_commits.description: Sign the commits with the project's signing key.

visibility.description: For a new repository. Default private. public needs the repository's name typed in repo.publish's confirm.

host.description: The web host: github.com, or your Forgejo or Gitea host.

login.description: The account the token belongs to, as the host reported it.

already_registered.description: The project already has a remote at this address: publish reuses it and pushes.

code.description: name_taken, repo_not_found, repo_not_empty, read_only, archived, public_full_mirror, secret_in_tree, mirror_not_ready, too_many_remotes, no_signing_key, no_secret_key, nothing_to_push, remote_differs.

empty.description: The repository has no refs at all.

files.description: The files the first push would hold (at most 300 are listed; file_count is all).

findings.description: Anything that looks like a secret in what would be pushed; each is a blocker.

path.description: The file (or the document, for a title).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the content that matched. git.remote.secret_ack covers exactly this file and content.

include_cover.description: The first push carries the project's own cover.

needs_confirm.description: The repository is public, or a public audience carries the cover: repo.publish needs confirm, the name typed exactly.

plan_token.description: Give it to repo.publish with the same fields.

remote_name.description: The name the remote will have in the project.

url.description: The address of the repository's Git endpoint, as the remote will hold it.

web_url.description: The repository's page at the host.

requests.description: What publishing will do, in order: create_repository, register_remote, push.

withheld.description: Documents a public remote does not carry, and why.

path.description: The document's path in the mirror.

ops.name: repo.publish
ops.desc: Publish the project to a repository: create it (or take an empty one), register it as a remote of the project and queue the first push. Needs the plan_token of repo.plan for the same fields, and for a public repository its name typed in confirm. Owner only, browser session only: an API key of any scope is refused. If the repository was created and a later step failed, the error says so and the call can be repeated with mode existing.

confirm.description: For a public repository, or a public audience with include_cover: the repository's name, typed exactly.

plan_token.description: The token repo.plan returned for exactly these fields. The call refuses (409 plan_changed) when anything the plan covered is different now: the settings, the files that would be pushed, what is withheld.

created.description: The repository was created by this call.

push.description: The queued first push; read git.push_get for its outcome.

bundle.description: For a force push: the bundle of the overwritten remote ref, in data/backups/git/.

documents.description: Documents the commit added, changed or removed, with the word change.

words.description: The change in words: positive for added text, negative for removed.

manifest.description: Only from git.push_get: path to SHA-256 of every file the commit holds.

outcome.description: pushed, up_to_date, or the error code.

remote_commits.description: For a rejected push: the remote's commits that are not ours.

subject.description: First line of the commit message.

remote_sha.description: The remote branch's head before this push.

subject.description: The commit's first line.

acknowledged.description: Findings of the pre-push check the owner acknowledged, each for one file with one content.

audience.description: public: only what a reader of the book sees. private: the full mirror.

exposed.description: The remote is public, was made by the publish flow, or sits at an address that was ever public: a change that lets more reach it needs a person at a browser and its name typed.

has_secret.description: A deploy key or token is stored. It is never returned.

host.description: The host the address points at.

host_key.description: The accepted host key; absent until one is accepted.

fingerprint.description: SHA256:... of the accepted host key.

include_cover.description: The push carries the project's own cover (the layout and its pictures). On for a private remote; off for a public one until a person turns it on.

interval_minutes.description: Minutes between pushes when push_mode is interval.

key_fingerprint.description: SHA256:... of the deploy key, as the host shows it.

only_done.description: A public remote carries only documents whose status is done.

path_prefix.description: Subdirectory of the repository the files are placed in.

public_key.description: The deploy key's public half, an authorized_keys line to add to the repository with write access.

restore_paused.description: A restore paused this remote. Only the owner switching it on lifts that: no check, test or restart does.

setup.description: What is still needed before anything can be pushed: deploy_key, host_key, token. Empty when ready.

sign_commits.description: Commits of this remote are signed with the project's signing key.

behind.description: A local commit has not reached the remote.

in_sync.description: The remote has the newest commit and nothing is waiting or running.

last_commit_sha.description: The newest commit the remote is known to have.

last_error.description: Written for a person; never contains a credential.

last_error_code.description: A stable code: host_key_unpinned, host_key_changed, auth_failed, repo_not_found, unreachable, timeout, remote_ahead, rejected_by_remote, secret_in_tree, credentials_unreadable, no_mirror, mirror_off, bundle_failed, too_large, paused_by_restore.

last_push_at.description: When a commit last reached the remote.

local_sha.description: The newest commit in the local repository.

mirror_on.description: The Markdown mirror is running; pushes are built from it.

next_attempt_at.description: When an automatic retry may run after a failure.

rejected.description: Present when state is rejected: what is on the remote.

commits.description: The remote's newest commits that this project did not make, newest first (at most 20).

subject.description: First line of the commit message.

remote_sha.description: The remote branch's head as last observed.

running.description: A push is queued or running now.

secrets.description: Present when the last push was refused for something that looks like a secret: the files and the SHA-256 of what matched. The owner can acknowledge one with git.remote.secret_ack.

path.description: The file (or the document, for a title).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the content that matched. git.remote.secret_ack covers exactly this file and content.

state.description: new: nothing pushed yet. synced: the remote has the newest commit. behind: a commit waits locally (the remote was unreachable or the push failed) and is retried with backoff. rejected: the remote has commits that are not ours; nothing is pushed until the writer force-pushes or imports. blocked: a person must act (credentials, host key, a secret in the text).

trigger.description: The push trigger, when the remote has one: where it calls and how the last delivery went. Never its secret or the address's path.

last_status.description: A short line about the last delivery, never a response body.

origin.description: The address's scheme, host and port. Its path and query are stored encrypted and not shown.

pending.description: Deliveries waiting for a retry.

secret_hint.description: The start of the signing secret, to tell two apart. The secret itself is shown once, when it is made or rotated.

username.description: The user name that goes with an HTTPS token.

url.description: The address of the repository's Git endpoint, as the remote will hold it.

web_url.description: The repository's page at the host.

ops.name: repo.release
ops.desc: Publish a compiled edition (EPUB, DOCX, PDF or a Markdown bundle) as a release asset at a GitHub or Forgejo remote, after a successful push: a release for the tag at the commit the remote has, the file as an asset, the manifest hash and the file's SHA-256 in the notes. Runs as a job; read repo.release_get. A retry with the same tag and manifest hash adds no second asset; a tag that already has another edition is refused. The file holds what a reader sees and is capped (64 MB). Owner only, browser session only.

format.description: epub (EPUB 3), docx (styled reading copy), pdf (a print PDF), md (plain Markdown) or md_bundle (the Markdown files a public remote carries, with their pictures, as a zip). None carries notes, private notes, ghosted text, alternatives or the author's contact block.

preset.description: For pdf: print-6x9 (default), print-5.5x8.5, print-5x8, print-a5, proof-letter or proof-a4.

preview.description: Say what would happen (the repository, the tag, the commit, whether the release exists) and change nothing.

remote_id.description: The remote. Optional while the project has exactly one.

tag.description: The release's tag, like v1.0. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, up to 64.

forced_options.description: Options held to what a reader sees whatever the preset says.

commit_sha.description: The commit the tag points at.

input_hash.description: The compile's manifest hash, in the release notes.

release_url.description: The release's page at the host.

reused.description: The asset was already at the host (a retry): nothing was uploaded.

ops.name: repo.release_get
ops.desc: One release attempt: its status, the asset, the hashes, and why it failed. Owner only.

commit_sha.description: The commit the tag points at.

input_hash.description: The compile's manifest hash, in the release notes.

release_url.description: The release's page at the host.

reused.description: The asset was already at the host (a retry): nothing was uploaded.

ops.name: repo.release_list
ops.desc: A remote's release attempts, newest first (the last 30). Owner only.

remote_id.description: The remote. Optional while the project has exactly one.

commit_sha.description: The commit the tag points at.

input_hash.description: The compile's manifest hash, in the release notes.

release_url.description: The release's page at the host.

reused.description: The asset was already at the host (a retry): nothing was uploaded.

ops.name: review.queue
ops.desc: The writer's review queue: every open thread of the project in reading order (comments on the project first; then each document in the order of the book, its threads in order of position, those that lost their text last), each with its document and breadcrumb, plus the counts per document. Give after (a thread id, even one just resolved) to get the threads that come after it: the first is the next unresolved. Filter by document_id, author, kind and state. Needs the editor role.

ops.name: stats.project
ops.desc: Progress toward the project's total words: the target, the words per day pace, the words per day needed for a deadline, and a projected finish date only when there is enough recent writing to project from.

days_left.description: Days from today to the deadline, counting today; 0 when there is no deadline or it has passed.

deadline.description: The caller's own deadline if set, else the project's; empty for none.

percent.description: Words as a percentage of the target; may exceed 100.

projected_date.description: When the target would be reached at the recent net pace. Present only when the pace window holds enough writing days to say; absent is the honest answer otherwise.

required_per_day.description: Net words a day to reach the target by the deadline; 0 when there is none to reach.

target.description: The target words are measured against: the caller's own project goal if set, else the project's shared word goal; 0 for none.

target_source.description: goal: the caller's own; project: the shared word goal; empty: none.

words.description: Words in the project's live documents.

writing_days.description: Days with words added in the pace window.

ops.name: stats.today
ops.desc: The caller's day so far on a project: words added and net, minutes, the daily target, whether it is met, and the streak. Per person: other members' numbers are never visible.

minutes.description: Active writing time, from the gaps between saves.

remaining.description: Words still to add to meet the target, 0 once met.

streak.description: Consecutive days the goal was met, counting today once it is met. Today does not break it until the day ends.

target.description: Today's daily target, 0 when there is no goal.

words_added.description: Words added today. This is what the goal counts.

words_net.description: New words minus old words today; negative on a day of cutting. Shown beside the goal, never against it.

ops.name: studio.calendar
ops.desc: The caller's activity calendar: columns of seven days, Monday first, with month labels, Monday-Wednesday-Friday row labels and five intensity steps read from the caller's own writing days. An empty day is empty; nothing is marked missed. Use all=true for all of the caller's writing.

all.description: All the person's writing, never fewer than 24 weeks.

label_rows.description: The rows that carry a weekday label: Monday, Wednesday and Friday (0, 2, 4). Weekday names are the keys studio.weekday.0 to studio.weekday.6.

cuts.description: The words of the 25th, 50th and 75th percentile of the person's own writing days (nearest rank): a day above the third cut is step 4, above the second step 3, above the first step 2, otherwise step 1.

days.description: How many writing days the cuts were read from.

uniform.description: Every writing day has the same words, so every writing day is step 4.

weeks.description: Columns of seven days, Monday first, oldest first; the last column holds today.

future.description: After today: not a day yet.

hit.description: A daily goal in force that day was met.

level.description: 0 for an empty day, 1 to 4 by the thresholds.

month.description: 1 to 12 on the first column of a month (the column holding its first day), else absent: the month label.

start.description: The Monday.

words.description: Words added in the window.

writing_days.description: Days in the window with words added.

b_project.description: Only this project's words in B. Two projects over the same dates are two drafts.

preset.description: A against B, over finished days of the same number: the days of this week before today against the same days of last week, the days of this month before today against the same days of last month (the first days, when last month was shorter), the 30 days before today against the 30 before them. Today is not in the comparison. Instead of the dates.

net.description: New words minus old words, shown beside the words added and never against them.

words.description: Words added: what goals count.

days.description: How many days the side spans, from and to included. Differences between two sides of different lengths say little; a page leaves them out.

words.description: Words added: what goals count.

days.description: How many days the side spans, from and to included. Differences between two sides of different lengths say little; a page leaves them out.

compared.description: False when A is a period with no finished day yet (a Monday, the 1st of a month): A is shown so far, B is empty, the differences are 0 and mean nothing, and a note says the comparison starts tomorrow.

words.description: A against B.

ops.desc: The writing dashboard in one read, for the caller only: today's words against the daily target, the habit-streak card, the goals with counts, the four period cards with deltas and sparklines, the words-written series with the busiest weekdays and hours, the 24-week activity calendar, the person's own words per project, the three-week trend, a few gentle nudges as message keys, and the running sprint. Every figure counts words added (net words are beside them, never against a day), is summed from the projects the caller may read and has unlocked, and is computed on this server. ops.desc: Accept a suggestion: apply all of its changes to the document in one transaction, as one history entry with reason suggestion-accepted (restoring the entry before undoes it), with no word credit. ops.desc: List the project's webhooks with their state: enabled, last status, deliveries waiting and dead. Never includes a secret. Project owner.

events.description: Every event a webhook can subscribe to.

dead.description: Deliveries that failed for good and are listed in webhook.deliveries.

disabled_reason.description: Why it was switched off, when the server did it.

failure_streak.description: Deliveries in a row that died. The webhook is switched off at 10.

include_text.description: Whether comment.created carries the comment's words.

last_status.description: The HTTP status of the last attempt, 0 when it never got an answer.

pending.description: Deliveries waiting to be sent or retried.

previous_secret_live.description: True while a rotated secret still signs deliveries beside the new one.

secret_hint.description: The start of the signing secret, to tell secrets apart. The secret itself is shown once.

url.description: Where it sends: scheme, host and port only. The path and query of the address are sealed with the server's secret key and never shown again (they may be a secret); send a new url to replace the whole address.

url_path_set.description: True when the address has a path or query (stored sealed).

ops.name: webhook.redeliver
ops.desc: Queue a dead or delivered notification again, with the same delivery id. Project owner.

error.description: The kind of failure of the last attempt: blocked, timeout, dns, refused, tls, network, redirect_refused, rejected, server_error, rate_limited or gone.

excerpt.description: A few words of a failing response, cleaned: no markup, no line breaks, 160 characters.

id.description: Sent as the Scriobh-Webhook-Id header on every attempt: store the ids you have seen to apply an event once.

next_attempt_at.description: When a pending delivery is due.

status.description: The HTTP status of the last attempt, 0 when it never got an answer.

ops.name: webhook.rotate_secret
ops.desc: Replace the signing secret. The new secret is in this response and nowhere else; the old one keeps signing beside it for keep_old_hours so a receiver can change over. Project owner.

keep_old_hours.description: How long the old secret keeps signing beside the new one, so a receiver can change over without a gap. Default 24; 0 for none; at most 168.

secret.description: The signing secret. Shown once; store it now. Every delivery carries Scriobh-Webhook-Signature: v1=hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + body)), with the timestamp in Scriobh-Webhook-Timestamp; reject a delivery whose signature does not match or whose timestamp is more than five minutes off.

ops.name: webhook.test
ops.desc: Send a signed ping to the webhook's address now and report what came back (status and failure kind). It is recorded in the deliveries and never retried. At most one every five seconds. Project owner.

ops.name: webhook.update
ops.desc: Change a webhook's name, address, events, whether comments carry their words, or switch it on or off. Project owner.

enabled.description: Switch it off or on. Switching it on clears a reason it was switched off and the failure count.

include_text.description: WARNING: true sends the words of each new comment out of the instance.

url.description: A new address, replacing the whole of the old one (the old path and query are never shown, so they cannot be edited). The failure count starts again.
